cells.Set by: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
cells.Values and default: Name of an LSF queue. The script passes the text to `bsub -q` without a check. Unset: the queue `sw-build`.
cells.Effect: Selects the LSF queue that receives the build job. `make` runs `bin/bsub-build` only when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.

cells.Set by: A developer, for one `make` test run.
cells.Values and default: Name of one worker host (a server that LSF runs remote tests on), for example `andoria-02`. More than 1 word stops `make` with an error. `make REMOTE_HOST=name` also works. Unset: `make` requests no worker host.
cells.Effect: `make` adds `--remote-host=<value>` to the `bin/slice run` command of the targets `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`. Slice then requires that worker host for the remote run. It needs the remote mode `1`, `sku0` or `sku1` (the value of `REMOTE`). With the mode `0`, `make` stops with an error for every goal. `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` supplies a mode only for the goals that its row names. The remote build job does not receive it.

cells.Set by: A developer, for one `make` test run.
cells.Values and default: One CPU model name that OpenLava (the LSF scheduler for remote test runs) knows, for example `genoa96`. More than 1 word stops `make`. `make REMOTE_MODEL=name` also works. Unset: `make` requests no CPU model.
cells.Effect: `make` adds `--remote-model=<value>` to the `bin/slice run` command of the targets `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`. Slice then requires that CPU model for the remote run. It needs the remote mode `1` (the value of `REMOTE`). With the mode `0`, `make` stops with an error for every goal. With `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` stops with the error `already selects a pool class`. The remote build job does not receive it.

cells.Set by: No one. `GNUmakefile` rejects it. A test checks the error.
cells.Values and default: Any text that is not blank. The text is not parsed. `make REMOTE_PREFER=value` has the same effect. Unset: no effect.
cells.Effect: `make` stops for every goal with the error `REMOTE_REQUIRE and REMOTE_PREFER are not supported`. `GNUmakefile` only tests that the value is not blank. The error text names the supported inputs: `REMOTE=sku0`, `REMOTE=sku1`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `REMOTE_HOST`.

cells.Set by: No one. `GNUmakefile` rejects it. A test checks the error.
cells.Values and default: Any text that is not blank. The text is not parsed. `make REMOTE_REQUIRE=value` has the same effect. Unset: no effect.
cells.Effect: `make` stops for every goal with the error `REMOTE_REQUIRE and REMOTE_PREFER are not supported`. `GNUmakefile` only tests that the value is not blank. The error text names the supported inputs: `REMOTE=sku0`, `REMOTE=sku1`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `REMOTE_HOST`.

cells.Set by: The shell profile of a shared development machine.
cells.Values and default: One of `0`, `1`, `sku0`, `sku1`. `sku0` and `sku1` act as `1` and also select one CPU model for remote test runs. Other text stops `make`. `make TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1` also works. Unset: `0`, builds and tests run on the local machine. Empty: `make` stops with an error when it uses the value.
cells.Effect: `make` copies it to an undefined `REMOTE` when a goal is a build goal, a Slice test goal, or a goal in `REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED_TEST_GOALS`. `make` without a goal counts as the build goal `all`. With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, builds and Slice tests run on LSF workers. The build goals are `all`, `build`, `core`, `build-core`, `build-prod`, `build-test`, `build-ingest`, `build-test-host`, `build-test-fpga`. The Slice test goals are `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga`, `test-fast`. With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` stops for a goal in `REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED_TEST_GOALS`, for example `test-proxy`. Other goals ignore it. `REMOTE` overrides it.

hints.problem: Two descriptions of `sku0` and `sku1` in neighbouring rows. Text A, in `REMOTE`: "`sku0` and `sku1` also add `--remote-sku=<value>` (a server class of the test pool)". Text B, in `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION`: "`sku0` and `sku1` act as `1` and also select one CPU model for remote test runs." A is the right wording. The repository calls them pool classes, and `REMOTE_MODEL` is the separate control for an exact CPU model (its row quotes the error `already selects a pool class`). B is true today only: each class maps to one CPU model now.
hints.suggested: In `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION`, replace "`sku0` and `sku1` act as `1` and also select one CPU model for remote test runs." with "`sku0` and `sku1` act as `1` and also select one server class of the test pool for remote test runs."

cells.Set by: `flake.nix`, for the Nix dev shell and the Nix CMake builds.
cells.Values and default: Directory path. CMake searches it for the library `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64`. The Nix files set `${llvm19.compiler-rt}/lib/linux`. Unset: CMake searches only `/usr/lib/llvm-19/lib/clang/19/lib/linux`.
cells.Effect: CMake searches this directory for the compiler-rt builtins library (an LLVM runtime library) before `/usr/lib/llvm-19/lib/clang/19/lib/linux`. CMake links the library that it finds into libtron. Configure stops with the error `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64 library not found` when neither directory holds the library. `find_library` uses `NO_DEFAULT_PATH`. CMake searches no other directory. CMake keeps the result in the cache variable `COMPILER_RT_BUILTINS`. A build tree that already holds a result does not search again.

cells.Set by: Nothing. The script sets it for the option `--remove-global`.
cells.Values and default: Any text that is not empty. The text is not parsed. `0` also turns it on. Unset: the script continues with its normal Rust check.
cells.Effect: The script acts as if `--remove-global` was given, and then exits. Without root rights it prints an error and exits with code 1. As root, when `dpkg` reports a `rustc` package, it runs `apt-get remove --purge -y rustc cargo librust-std*` and `apt-get autoremove -y`. The script does not reset the variable at its start. CMake runs the script at configure time. With a value set, a configure without root rights fails with `Failed to set up Rust`. A configure by root removes the packages and skips the Rust check.

cells.Set by: Nothing. The script sets it for the option `--user`.
cells.Values and default: Any text that is not empty. The text is not parsed. `0` also turns it on. Unset: the script continues with its normal Rust check.
cells.Effect: The script acts as if `--user` was given. It installs Rust in `$HOME/.cargo` when none exists, or upgrades the Rust there when its version differs from `rust-toolchain.toml`. Then it exits and does not write `rust/rustenv` (the file that tells `rust/run-cargo` which Rust to use outside Nix). The script does not reset the variable at its start. CMake runs the script at configure time. So an environment value changes that configure, also inside the Nix dev shell. The script tests `REMOVE_GLOBAL` first. A new install downloads `rustup-init` from `static.rust-lang.org`.

cells.Read by: The shell hook of the Nix dev shell (`flake.nix`)
cells.Set by: The Nix dev shell hook. No person sets it.
cells.Values and default: A user name. On x86_64 Linux the hook sets it from `id -un` and replaces a value from the caller. Unset: the hook sets it on x86_64 Linux. On other systems the hook does not use it.
cells.Effect: The hook stores the output of `id -un` in it at its start. At its end the hook puts `(nix) ` before the prompt text `PS1` and replaces `\u` in `PS1` with the name. Then the hook unsets the variable. It is a temporary variable of the hook. The hook exports it, and programs that the hook starts receive it. When `id -un` prints nothing, the hook does not change `PS1`, and the variable stays set and empty.

cells.Read by: Nothing in Tron. `flake.nix` exports it in the Nix dev shell and in the Nix CMake builds (`tron-cmake-test-build`, `cmake-sandbox`).
cells.Set by: `flake.nix`, for the Nix dev shell and the Nix CMake builds.
cells.Values and default: Directory path in the Nix store: `${llvm19.clang}/resource-root`. On macOS the Nix dev shell sets empty text. Unset: nothing changes. No file in the repository reads this name.
cells.Effect: Nothing changes in Tron. No file in the repository reads this name.

cells.Read by: Nothing in Tron. `flake.nix` exports it in the Nix dev shell.
cells.Values and default: Path of the `clang-19` wrapper program in the Nix store. Unset: nothing changes. No file in the repository reads the environment variable.
cells.Effect: Nothing changes in Tron. No file in the repository reads the environment variable. `CMakePresets.json` sets the CMake cache variable of the same name to `clang-19`, and that is a separate setting. The Nix dev shell also sets `CC` to the same path.
